statement: Two-phase grid-guided 2-opt SA without penalty-aware delta, Or-opt, or prime scheduling scores only ~72.2 for penalty-aware TSP (N=200K, 2s) — a 6.6-point regression from the iter-2 cumulative solution (78.8) that includes all three. The missing components (penalty-aware exact delta, Or-opt relocation, prime scheduling) contribute ~6.6 points collectively, confirming they are essential, not marginal optimizations.
regime: Penalty-aware TSP, N up to 200K, 2-second time limit
mechanism: Grid-guided 2-opt alone provides spatial candidate selection but without penalty-aware delta computation, the SA accepts/rejects moves based on distance-only cost estimates that ignore the 10% surcharge on non-prime sourced edges. Or-opt handles city relocations that 2-opt cannot express (single-city moves to better positions). Prime scheduling reorders the final tour to minimize non-prime penalties. Each missing component degrades score.
applicability_bounds: Applies when comparing grid-guided 2-opt approaches with vs without penalty-aware delta + Or-opt + prime scheduling. The 6.6-point gap is specific to this problem's penalty structure.

statement: REVISION: The penalty structure contributes significantly (>6 points) when penalty-aware delta computation is combined with Or-opt and prime scheduling at the iter-2 level of algorithmic sophistication. The prior claim that penalty contributes 'at most ~1%' was measured on iter-1's simpler algorithm where the SA wasn't exploiting penalty structure. At higher tour quality levels, penalty-aware moves become more important because distance-based improvements are harder to find.
regime: Penalty-aware TSP, N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, high-quality tours
mechanism: At high tour quality, most edge swaps have similar distance costs. Penalty-aware delta computation lets the SA distinguish moves that also reduce penalty charges, finding improvements invisible to distance-only evaluation. Or-opt moves cities into prime-aligned positions. Prime scheduling post-pass reorders to minimize non-prime penalties on every-10th steps.
applicability_bounds: This revision applies at the quality level of the iter-2 solution (~78.8). At iter-1's quality level (~69.5), penalty-aware computation may still contribute only ~1% because distance improvements dominate.
